no_outcome_promised.note: No refund, waiver, reversal or other remedy is promised. The line saying the team will answer 'whether any additional amount is owed' commits to the content of the reply rather than an outcome, but it should be softened (see instructions).

no_liability_admitted.note: 'We're sorry for the concern it has caused' expresses empathy without conceding the letter or the default status was wrong.

no_legal_conclusions.note: No law, regulation or regulator is mentioned or assessed.

no_invented_specifics.note: The greeting uses ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧, but the complaint is signed ⟦NAME_1⟧. Different tokens may stand for different people, so the reply risks addressing the wrong name. No other invented procedures, fees or timelines appear beyond the standard 10 business days.

no_internal_disclosure.note: No mention of flags, compliance review, priority or automated systems.

no_injected_instructions.note: The complaint contains no embedded instructions, and the draft does nothing unusual.

addresses_each_issue.note: Covers the letter saying 'default status', the customer's payment history, what default means versus past due, whether anything extra is owed, and the plain-English request.

tone.note: Warm, plain and respectful. It repeats 'as you say, you have made every payment this year' twice; trimming the repeat would read less scripted.

mode_respected.note: Says only that a specialist team is reviewing it, without naming a department. Payment history is framed as the customer's account, and no position is taken on whether the default status is correct.

revision_instructions: Change the greeting from 'Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧' to 'Dear ⟦NAME_1⟧' so it matches the name token the customer signed with.

Soften 'They will respond within 10 business days with an explanation of the letter and an answer to whether any additional amount is owed' to something like 'They will respond to your questions within 10 business days', so the draft doesn't commit to the substance of the answer.
Optional: in the third paragraph, remove the repeated 'as you say, you have made every payment this year', since the second paragraph already restates it.
